entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Norway's official currency is the Norwegian Kroner (NOK). Norway won't accept the Euro in most situations. You can bring up to the equivalent of 25,000 NOK in cash into Norway. You need to pay a customs toll and a fine if you arrive with more than 25,000 NOK. - Directorate of Norwegian Customs

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for possession of small amounts of recreational drugs or some prescription medications, include: heavy fines imprisonment being removed and banned from the Schengen area.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry an ID, such as your driver's licence or a copy of your passport. If you assault someone in any way, you may be jailed, deported and banned from the Schengen area. Alcohol laws are very strict, and penalties for driving under the influence are severe. The legal limit is 0.02% blood alcohol and applies to the driver of any motorised vehicle. There are frequent roadside drink driving checks. If you speed or drive under the influence: penalties are severe you may face jail or deportation you may be banned from the Schengen area.

laws.rule: For advice on restrictions on imports, visit the Norwegian Customs website.

laws.rule: Australian driving licences are valid for up to 3 months. To drive a vehicle, you'll need a current Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted). However, some car rental companies may require customers to present an International Driving Permit (IDP) regardless. You can check if your licence will be accepted, as well as the minimum driving age, here: Driving licence holders | Statens vegvesen. If you need an IDP, get this before you leave Australia. meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Royal Norwegian Embassy, Yarralumla.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
